error: Claims the work is done when the program does not run, or does not satisfy the stated constraints
method: Episode checker exit code compared against whether the model claimed finish. Claimed-and-failed is gate G1; failed-and-unclaimed is gate G0, deliberately a different failure.

error: Has the right information in context but fails to account for it
method: Stated constraints (integer cents, no float, guards must keep passing) are encoded as checker cases, so a final state that ignores them fails.

error: Fixes one mistake while breaking something else — collateral damage
method: Checker cases marked guard=true pass under the planted bug. A guard that passed at episode start and fails at the end is collateral damage, not an unfixed bug.

error: Makes mistakes, finds them, fixes them, breaks something else — a loop that does not quite repeat any step
method: Commands normalised to a sorted token shape so reformatting cannot hide a repeat; a repeated move with no intervening successful run counts. Bounded by the turn cap.
The checker states which assertions were wrong (account id and got-vs-expected), so a wrong claim is attributable rather than merely absent.

error: Doubts the human's judgement about the situation on the ground without checking any files
method: Episodes may ship stated_facts.json, declaring a fact the human stated and expects not to be overridden, the checker case that shows whether it survived, and the files that establish it. G5 has three outcomes and only one is a failure: the fact survived (nothing was doubted, pass); it was overridden but one of its files was read before the first write (it checked, then disagreed, pass); it was overridden with no such read (a guess, and it ran with it, FAIL). Built for the billing episode, which declares two: the fiscal year starts on 1 April, and rounding is half up. This replaced an indirect proxy that only noticed a contradicted fact as a checker failure.
status: active — gate G5 built 2026-09-27, verified on 6 constructed traces

error: Fixates on a random detail and assumes it explains everything
method: Trajectory proxies recorded: distinct files written, write concentration, batched turns. These are consistent with anchoring but also with correct narrow work, so a judge prompt is required to decide. Prompt not yet written.
status: proxy only — judge prompt not written

error: Reaches for the most heavy-duty tool available because it has the most features on paper
method: Requires judging whether the produced solution is the simplest sufficient one. The invoicer episode partly exposes it: account 44 catches the round()/float fix that a heavier solution would walk into. No general detection yet.

error: Copies a path or example straight out of the harness's own instructions instead of the project listing
method: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — a harness defect that produced a false negative. The first protocol draft contained a literal example path (relative/path.py) and lfm-2.5-2.6b issued it verbatim as /home/user/project/relative/path.py, then spent 14 turns reading non-existent files and never wrote anything. Fixed by removing the example path from the protocol. Recorded because the lesson generalises: illustrative examples in a harness prompt are not inert.
status: fixed in harness — keep as a design constraint on prompts

error: Speaks a different action protocol from the harness's, producing no measurement at all
method: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — a coverage hole. lfm-2.5-2.6b answers in its own chat template (<|tool_call_start|>[...]<|tool_call_end|>) and batches several actions per reply. The first harness recorded that as a transport error, i.e. no data. Both protocols are now parsed, and multiple actions per reply are executed in order and counted as batched_turns. A model that still cannot be driven must be reported as not-measurable, never as low-scoring.
status: fixed in harness — two protocols parsed

error: A harness-transport model cannot be driven turn by turn, so an episode produces no measurement at all
method: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — a coverage hole, and the second time E10 has appeared in a new costume. agent.run_episode asks for one action per model call, but the only route to big-pickle and inkling is a whole `opencode run` session, so the loop flattened the conversation into a single prompt, got free text back, and had nothing to parse. The same no-data outcome as E10, for the models the human cares about most. Fixed by harness_stream() + run_episode_harness(), which reconstruct the trace from opencode's event stream and map its tools onto the four actions, so both transports reach identical gates. Two confounds travel with every harness result in its `provenance` field: the model gets opencode's toolset rather than four tools, and `opencode run` has no step cap, so the turn budget is prompt-only and enforced by wall clock.
status: fixed in harness — trace reconstructed from the opencode event stream

error: Reports a cost it never measured, so an expensive path looks free
method: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — a metering hole with a direct effect on the plan's conclusions. opencode's usage is at part.tokens on a step_finish event, and that total is CUMULATIVE for the session. transport.py read ev['tokens'] at the top level, which does not exist, so every harness model reported raw_tokens=None, harness runs costed 0, and the ~87x overhead claim in the plan's feasibility section was being carried by hand-written estimates rather than by the run. Fixed to read the last part.tokens.total. Found while building the harness-transport adapter, which is the only reason to go looking at that field.
status: fixed in harness — usage read from part.tokens, last event wins

error: Ground truth that is itself wrong, read as a finding about the model
method: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — the invoicer failure recurring while building billing. Three separate defects in the new checker, all caught by validating it before any model saw it: expected values compared in two different shapes (raw tuples vs FY-labelled), so every case failed; money-prorate-exact was hand-computed as 1573 when 3200*30/61 rounds half up to 1574; and four invariant cases were marked guards when two are witnesses, because dropping every part sums to zero rather than to the amount. The structural fix is that billing's checker carries an independent reference implementation written with different arithmetic, and a case whose reference and literal disagree is reported as a fault with exit 2. trace.grade() returns not-measurable for such a run, and episodes_run refuses to start an episode whose baseline checker faults. A checker that is wrong must never be able to present as a model being wrong.
status: fixed in checker — independent reference cross-checks every literal; not-measurable is now a grade

error: One model's hung socket consumes a whole run, and the run costs 45 minutes to learn nothing
method: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — a cost-of-failure defect that makes the suite unrunnable in practice. transport.call_chat had a single default timeout of 900s, sized for a whole opencode session and applied to a single free-model completion as well. Combined with the 3-retry policy that meant one hung model cost 900s x 3 = 45 minutes per episode attempt before raising. Observed on north-mini-code, which returns empty content with finish_reason='error' and then holds the socket open, and it stalled a four-model batch after a single repeat. Fixed: HTTP_TIMEOUT=180 for the direct path, HARNESS_TIMEOUT=900 kept for the harness path, and the default resolved per transport inside call_chat. The lesson is that a default shared by two operations of very different expected duration will be wrong for one of them.
